generations.prompt: A handcrafted miniature stop-motion film, vertical 9:16 composition. Macro lens, beautifully tactile materials, subtle stop-motion cadence, shallow depth of field. Inside a tiny vintage laundromat, mint-green tile wall, buttery yellow light. A single oval yellow enamel laundry basin sits on a wooden counter in the lower half of the frame. Exactly ONE small charcoal-gray cotton-wool storm cloud floats just above the basin, already present at the beginning. Thin silver threads of rain trickle steadily from the cloud into the basin; tiny ripples form. The cloud gives one very small disgruntled rumble and a brief soft internal flicker, then keeps raining. Camera makes a very slow straight push in. Charming, melancholy, spare composition, museum-quality practical miniature, no people, no hands, no faces on the cloud, no other clouds, no lettering, no captions, no logos. One uninterrupted shot. Sound: delicate water drops into an enamel bowl and a tiny muffled thunder grumble, quiet room tone, no music, no speech.
